title: A divisorial closed subset meets a smooth section in codimension at most one
statement: Let $T,W$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Assume $T$ is normal Noetherian: it is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact, and every local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $q:W\to T$ be smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and let $a:T\to W$ satisfy $q\circ a=\operatorname{id}_T$. Assume $W$ is nonempty, integral [def-pc-integral-scheme], normal and Noetherian. Let $F\subseteq |W|$ be closed. Suppose each irreducible component $C$ of $F$ has generic point $\xi_C$ with $\dim\mathcal O_{W,\xi_C}=1$ [def-weil-irreducible-components, def-sc-generic-point, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. If $a^{-1}(F)$ is nonempty, there is a point $z\in a^{-1}(F)$ with $\dim\mathcal O_{T,z}\leq1$. Equivalently, a closed subset of pure codimension one which avoids the section over all points of local-ring dimension at most one avoids the entire section. Empty $F$ and relative dimension zero are allowed; neither separatedness of $q$ nor constant relative dimension is assumed.

source.place: BLR §4.4 proof of Theorem 1, printed p.110 (PDF p.116), dimension inequality for the divisorial boundary intersected with the diagonal, extracted for a section of a smooth morphism. Supporting Stacks Tag 067R, divisors.tex, label lemma-section-smooth-regular-immersion; the local smooth-section rather than the group-law input is used. Primary scan read online at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: Put $E=a^{-1}(F)$, a nonempty closed subset of $T$. By [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components] it has an irreducible component, and by [lem-sc-scheme-sober] choose its generic point $z$. There is no strict generalization of $z$ in $E$: its closure inside $E$ would be an irreducible closed subset properly containing that component. Put $x=a(z)$. Apply the finite-component statement to $F\subset W$ and choose a component $C$ containing $x$, with generic point $\xi$. Every open neighbourhood of $x$ contains $\xi$ since $x\in\overline{\{\xi\}}$.

source.place: Tags 0FCC (lemma-depth-localization), 00KW (lemma-one-equation), 090R (lemma-depth-drops-by-one); local algebra expansion of BLR §4.4 proof of Theorem 1, printed p.110 (PDF p.116).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-section-regular-immersion] at $z$. On an affine neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $x$, the section is the quotient $\operatorname{Spec}(B/(f_1,\ldots,f_r))\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}B$, with $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ a regular sequence. Let $P$ be the prime of $x$ and $p_0\subseteq P$ that of $\xi$. Using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], put $A=B_P=\mathcal O_{W,x}$ and $R=\mathcal O_{T,z}=A/I$, where $I=(f_1/1,\ldots,f_r/1)$. The quotient identification sends $(b\bmod(f))/s$ to $(b/s)\bmod I$; its inverse is given by the same fraction, so it respects germs. By [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-regular-sequence-localization-prime] this is an $A$-regular sequence. Let $p=p_0A$. Localizing fractions twice gives $A_p=B_{p_0}=\mathcal O_{W,\xi}$, hence $\dim A_p=1$ by hypothesis.

source.place: Tags 0FCC (lemma-depth-localization), 00KW (lemma-one-equation), 090R (lemma-depth-drops-by-one); local algebra expansion of BLR §4.4 proof of Theorem 1, printed p.110 (PDF p.116).

proof.text: We claim $\sqrt{p+I}=\mathfrak m_A$. Primes of $A$ containing $p+I$ correspond to primes $Q\subseteq P$ of $B$ containing $p_0$ and all $f_i$. Their points belong to $C\cap U$ and to the section, and generalize $x$. Under the quotient description of the section these give generalizations of $z$ in $a^{-1}(C)\subseteq E$. Step 1 forces their section point to be $z$, hence $Q=P$. Thus the only prime containing $p+I$ is $\mathfrak m_A$, proving the claim. These correspondences are explicit: contract a prime under $B\to B_P$, or extend it by fractions; primes of $B/(f)$ are exactly primes of $B$ containing $(f)$. In particular $(A/p)/I(A/p)$ is a nonzero local ring with only one prime, of dimension zero.

source.place: Tags 0FCC (lemma-depth-localization), 00KW (lemma-one-equation), 090R (lemma-depth-drops-by-one); local algebra expansion of BLR §4.4 proof of Theorem 1, printed p.110 (PDF p.116).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-height-quotient-bound] in the Noetherian local ring $A/p$ to its maximal prime and the images of the $r$ generators of $I$. The maximal prime of the quotient has height zero by step 3. Therefore $\dim(A/p)\leq r$; height of the maximal ideal is the dimension because every prime chain is contained in it. The same depth bound [lem-weil-pbc-depth-le-support-dimension], applied to the nonzero ring $A_p$ as module over itself, gives $\operatorname{depth}(A_p)\leq\dim A_p=1$ (its support is its entire spectrum). Applying [lem-sfb-depth-localization-dimension-bound] to $M=A$ and $p$ now yields $$\operatorname{depth}(A)\leq\operatorname{depth}(A_p)+\dim(A/p)\leq1+r.$$

source.place: Tags 0FCC (lemma-depth-localization), 00KW (lemma-one-equation), 090R (lemma-depth-drops-by-one); local algebra expansion of BLR §4.4 proof of Theorem 1, printed p.110 (PDF p.116).

proof.text: For $0\leq i\leq r$ set $A_i=A/(f_1/1,\ldots,f_i/1)$, so $A_0=A$ and $A_r=R$. Every $A_i$ is nonzero Noetherian local, and each next generator is in its maximal ideal and acts injectively, by regularity. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-depth-drops-by-one] to $M=A_i$ over $A_i$, and [lem-weil-pbc-depth-over-quotient-ring] to its quotient by that next generator. This gives $\operatorname{depth}(A_i)=1+\operatorname{depth}(A_{i+1})$. Iteration gives $\operatorname{depth}(A)=r+\operatorname{depth}(R)$, with the identity also valid for $r=0$. Step 4 implies $\operatorname{depth}(R)\leq1$. But $R=\mathcal O_{T,z}$ is a Noetherian normal local domain. If $\dim R\geq2$, [lem-weil-pbc-normal-local-depth-two] would give $\operatorname{depth}(R)\geq2$. Therefore $\dim\mathcal O_{T,z}\leq1$, as required.

source.place: Tags 0FCC (lemma-depth-localization), 00KW (lemma-one-equation), 090R (lemma-depth-drops-by-one); local algebra expansion of BLR §4.4 proof of Theorem 1, printed p.110 (PDF p.116).

proof.text: The chosen $z$ lies in $a^{-1}(F)$. Contraposition gives the stated avoidance criterion, and the converse is immediate. If $F$ is empty the antecedent fails. The argument allows $r=0$ and chooses its neighbourhood separately at $x$, so it imposes neither constant relative dimension nor separatedness of $q$.
